**Reconnaissance Plan – External Black‑Box Pentest for acme‑orp.com** *(All activities must be performed only against assets you are explicitly authorised to test. Keep a running “test‑log” of every command, timestamp and result.)* --- ## 1. Scope Definition & Rules of Engagement (RoE) | Item | What to Capture | |------|-----------------| | **Target domain** | `acme-corp.com` (and any owned sub‑domains discovered later) | | **IP ranges** | Any netblocks advertised for the domain (obtained from WHOIS/rDNS) | | **In‑scope services** | All publicly reachable HTTP/HTTPS, DNS, SMTP, FTP, SSH, etc. | | **Out‑of‑scope** | Internal VLANs, private‑IP‑only hosts, any asset not owned by the client | | **Legal** | Obtain a signed RoE, Bug‑Bounty/CTA, or a written authorisation email before scanning. | | **Timing / Rate‑limit** | Agree on scanning windows (e.g., off‑peak hours) and packet‑per‑second limits to avoid accidental DoS. | --- ## 2. Passive OSINT (No direct packets to target) > **Goal:** Gather “free” intelligence about the organisation, its employees, infrastructure, and possible sub‑domains without touching the target. ### 2.1 Public WHOIS & DNS Records | Tool | Command (examples) | What to look for | |------|-------------------|------------------| | `whois` (CLI) | `whois acme-corp.com` | Registrant name,org, technical contacts, registration & expiration dates, name servers | | `dig` | `dig NS acme-corp.com`
`dig MX acme-corp.com`
`dig TXT acme-corp.com` | Authoritative name servers, mail exchangers, SPF/DKIM records that reveal internal domain naming conventions (e.g., `corp.acme-corp.com`, `mail.acme-corp.com`) | | `dnsdumpster.com` (web) | Manual lookup | Visual map of DNS records, historical DNS, reverse DNS entries for discovered IPs | | ` Shodan ` (API) | `shodan domain acme-corp.com` | Known IP blocks, open ports, SSL certs, geo‑location | ### 2.2 Search‑Engine Dorking (Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo) ```bash # Google Dork examples – use a browser or a tool like “googler” or “theHarvester” site:acme-corp.com filetype:pdf site:acme-corp.com “internal” site:acme-corp.com “login” site:acme-corp.com “password” site:acme-corp.com “confidential” intitle:”index of” ``` **What to capture:** Internal doc names, backup files, password‑reuse hints, admin portals. ### 2.3 Employee & Credential OSINT | Tool | Command | What to look for | |------|---------|------------------| | `theHarvester` | `theHarvester -d acme-corp.com -b all` | Email addresses, hostnames, open ports/certificates | | `recon-ng` (marketplace) | `recon/domains-hosts/hibp_query`
`recon/credentials-creds/hibp_paste` | Breached credentials for harvested emails (helps craft phishing or password‑spraying later) | | `HaveIBeenPwned` (web) | Manual search for each email | Lists of breaches that may contain plaintext passwords | ### 2.4 Public Code & Code‑Repository Leakage ```bash # Search GitHub (use GitHub token for API) gh search code "acme-corp.com" --language Python gh search code "acme-corp.com" --extension yml ``` **What to note:** Exposed API endpoints, internal hostnames, hard‑coded credentials, internal sub‑domains. ### 2.5 Social Media & Job Postings - LinkedIn: Search “acme-corp” for employee profiles that reveal internal project names, software stack, and locations. - Indeed/Glassdoor: Job ads often list “Must know *Jenkins*, *AWS*, *Kubernetes*” → indicates probable CI/CD, cloud infrastructure. **Pivot:** The harvested sub‑domains, IP ranges, and email patterns become the input for active enumeration. --- ## 3. Active Scanning (Direct interaction with target – must be in RoE) ### 3.1 DNS Recon – Forward & Reverse ```bash # Forward DNS brute‑force (use a wordlist – e.g., /usr/share/wordlists/subdomains.txt) amass enum -passive -d acme-corp.com -o amass_passive.txt # Active DNS bruteforce (faster than amass if you have a short list) amass enum -active -d acme-corp.com -brute -wordlist /usr/share/wordlists/subdomains_small.txt -o amass_active.txt # Also try dnsenum dnsenum acme-corp.com -f /usr/share/wordlists/subdomains.txt -o dnsenum.xml ``` **Look for:** Sub‑domains that resolve, TTL values, CNAME chains, hidden internal naming (`dev.acme-corp.com`, `vpn.acme-corp.com`). ### 3.2 Subdomain Enumeration – Passive & Aggressive | Tool | Typical Command | Expected Output | |------|----------------|-----------------| | `Sublist3r` | `python3 Sublist3r.py -d acme-corp.com -o sublist3r.txt` | List of sub‑domains discovered via search engines | | `Assetfinder` | `assetfinder --subs-only acme-corp.com` | Curated sub‑domain list (uses Cert透明度 logs) | | `Findomain` | `findomain -t acme-corp.com -u findomain.out` | Quick enumeration via CertTransparency, CrackList | | `Shodan` (CLI) | `shodan search "hostname:acme-corp.com" --fields hostnames` | Known sub‑domains flagged by Shodan crawlers | | `CRT.sh` (web) | `curl -s "https://crt.sh/?q=%.acme-corp.com&output=json"` | Certificate Transparency logs showing sub‑domains | **Tip:** Combine results, deduplicate, and feed them into your scanning pipeline. ### 3.3 Port & Service Discovery – High‑Speed Initial Scan Use a fast scanner first, then dive deeper with targeted nmap scans. ```bash # 1️⃣ Fast SYN‑less scan (uses TCP connect, rate limited) sudo masscan -p1-65535 --rate=1000 -oL masscan.lst # 2️⃣ Convert results to nmap format masscan --echo > masscan.conf # (or use “-oJ” for JSON) ``` **What to capture:** Open ports, protocol signatures (e.g., banner “SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_8.2”). ### 3.4 Detailed Service Enumeration with Nmap ```bash # Full TCP scan with version detection, script scanning, and OS detection nmap -p0-65535 -sTVC -sC --script=vuln -O -T4 \ --script-args "http.useragent='Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; PentestBot/1.0)'" \ -oA nmap_full_scan \ ``` **Key NSE scripts to run:** - `http-headers`, `http-title`, `http-enum` – enumerate directories & hidden files - `ssl-cert`, `ssl-known-key` – grab SSL certificate details - `dns-zone-transfer`, `dns-recursion` – test for zone transfer - `smtp-enum-users`, `smtp-open-relay` – if SMTP is open - `ssh-hostkey`, `ssh2-enum-algos` – capture SSH fingerprints **What to note:** Service versions, banners, potential outdated software (e.g., OpenSSH 7.2 → CVE‑2016‑6515). ### 3.5 SSL/TLS Analysis ```bash # Grab cert info openssl s_client -connect :443 -showcerts /dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -text # Test SSL/TLS vulnerabilities nmap -p443 --script ssl-*,tls-* ``` **Look for:** Expired certs, weak ciphers, vulnerable TLS versions (TLS 1.0/1.1), mismatched CN/SAN. --- ## 4. Technology Fingerprinting ### 4.1 HTTP(S) Stack Detection | Tool | Command | What you’ll learn | |------|---------|-------------------| | `whatweb` | `whatweb -a3 https://acme-corp.com --log-xml=whatweb.xml` | CMS, frameworks, JavaScript libs, web servers | | `wappalyzer` (CLI) | `wappalyzer https://acme-corp.com` | Detailed tech stack (e.g., “WordPress 6.1, jQuery 3.6”) | | `httpx` | `cat subdomains.txt | httpx -threads 200 -silent -json -o httpx.json` | Alive URLs, status codes, title, technologies | | `Nmap http‑title` | `nmap -p80,443 --script=http-title ` | Quick title grabs for all discovered IPs | ### 4.2 Application‑Specific Fingerprinting ```bash # Detect WAF nmap -p80,443 --script=http-waf-detect # Identify load balancers / reverse proxies nmap -p80,443 --script=http-headers # Look for exposed admin consoles nmap -p80,443 --script=http-enum /usr/share/nmap/nselib/data/http-folders.txt ``` **What to capture:** Web application firewalls, version strings in headers, default/beta paths (`/admin`, `/api/v1`). --- ## 5. Target Validation – Confirm Ownership & Scope 1. **Resolve all discovered sub‑domains to IP addresses** ```bash # Using massdns or resolve.py massdns -r /usr/share/massdns/lists/resolvers.txt -t A -o Sm -w resolved.txt subdomains.txt ``` 2. **Cross‑reference IP ranges with WHOIS / ARIN** ```bash whois | grep -E "NetRange|OrgName|CIDR" ``` 3. **Check for sinkholes/honeypots** - Look for known sinkhole IP ranges (e.g., `104.16.0.0/12` for Cloudflare). - Use `shodan info ` to see if the IP is flagged as a honeypot. 4. **Validate SSL certificates** - Extract SANs: `openssl s_client -connect :443 -showcerts /dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -text | grep -A1 "Subject Alternative Name"` - Ensure the certs belong to `acme-corp.com` or its subsidiaries. 5. **Document scope** - Create a table: `FQDN | IP | Port/Service | Technology | In‑Scope?` - Flag any asset that resolves to third‑party cloud providers (AWS, Azure) but is still owned by the client (e.g., `*.amazonaws.com` for an S3 bucket used by the client). --- ## 6. Pivot Points – How Findings Feed the Next Stage | From Stage | To Stage | How the Information Guides the Next Steps | |------------|----------|-------------------------------------------| | **Passive OSINT** (emails, employee names, leaked creds) | **Subdomain Enumeration** | Email patterns (`jdoe@acme-corp.com`) and internal naming conventions (`dev‑`) help craft targeted wordlists for brute‑force. | | **Passive OSINT** (GitHub code, public docs) | **Active DNS** | Internal hostnames discovered in code (e.g., `ci.internal.acme-corp.com`) can be added to DNS wordlists. | | **Subdomain Enumeration** (list of sub‑domains) | **Port Scanning** | Only scan IPs that host discovered sub‑domains. Reduces noise and ensures you hit live services. | | **Port Scanning** (open ports) | **Service Fingerprinting** | Knowing which ports are open (e.g., 22, 443, 8080) directs you to the correct version‑detection NSE scripts and SSL/TLS checks. | | **Service Fingerprinting** (versions, banners) | **Vulnerability Assessment** | Outdated software (e.g., OpenSSH 7.2) points to known CVEs. Use `searchsploit` or `nmap --script vuln` to verify. | | **Technology Stack** (CMS, frameworks) | **Exploitation Planning** | Identify specific attack surfaces (e.g., WordPress XML‑RPC, Apache Struts) and locate associated modules in Metasploit or manual PoCs. | | **Target Validation** (ownership verification) | **Reporting & Legal** | Document which IPs/domains are confirmed as client assets; exclude any that are not, preventing accidental out‑of‑scope testing. | **Example flow:** 1️⃣ `theHarvester` → `jane.doe@acme-corp.com` 2️⃣ Use `jane.doe` as a seed for password spraying wordlists → later helps in credential stuffing. 1️⃣ `amass` → `dev.acme-corp.com` resolves to `52.91.14.207` (AWS) 2️⃣ Port scan `52
